extracted.intended_audience: national intellectual property / design offices, WIPO officials, policymakers, and practitioners involved in industrial-design classification and registration
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural standards establishing an international classification for industrial designs (the Locarno Agreement): what the classification must contain, how it is adopted/amended, institutional roles (Assembly, Committee of Experts, International Bureau), voting/notification/entry-into-force rules, and financial/administrative provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of Special Union and single classification
rubrics_metrics.description: The countries to which this Agreement applies constitute a Special Union and adopt a single classification for industrial designs ("the international classification").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the foundational instrument establishing a Special Union specifically for an international classification of industrial designs (Article 1(1)-(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of the international classification
rubrics_metrics.description: The international classification shall comprise: (i) a list of classes and subclasses; (ii) an alphabetical list of goods in which industrial designs are incorporated, with an indication of the classes and subclasses into which they fall; (iii) explanatory notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These three components are mandatory elements of the classification and form the structure used by Offices and the Committee of Experts (Article 1(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: List of classes and subclasses is annexed and amendable
rubrics_metrics.description: The list of classes and subclasses is the list annexed to the Agreement, subject to such amendments and additions as the Committee of Experts may make to it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Committee of Experts has authority to change classes and subclasses under the procedures of Article 3 (Article 1(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Alphabetical list of goods and explanatory notes adoption procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The alphabetical list of goods and the explanatory notes shall be adopted by the Committee of Experts in accordance with the procedure laid down in Article 3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adoption and amendment of these parts follow the Committee of Experts' procedural rules (Article 1(5)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to amend or supplement classification
rubrics_metrics.description: The international classification may be amended or supplemented by the Committee of Experts, in accordance with the procedure laid down in Article 3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee-driven updates are anticipated and governed by Article 3 procedures (Article 1(6)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Official languages of the classification
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) The international classification shall be established in the English and French languages. (b) Official texts in other languages may be established by the International Bureau after consultation with interested Governments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: English and French texts are equally authentic; other-language official texts require Assembly designation and consultation (Article 1(7)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative character and national legal scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to the Agreement's requirements, the international classification shall be solely of an administrative character; nevertheless each country may attribute to it the legal scope it considers appropriate, and the classification shall not bind countries as regards the nature and scope of protection afforded to designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Agreement does not impose uniform substantive protection; national Offices may treat classification as principal or subsidiary and decide legal implications (Article 2(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted use as principal or subsidiary system
rubrics_metrics.description: Each country of the Special Union reserves the right to use the international classification as a principal or as a subsidiary system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States may choose how central the international classification is to their national procedures (Article 2(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to include class/subclass numbers in official documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Offices shall include in the official documents for the deposit or registration of designs, and, if they are officially published, in the publications in question, the numbers of the classes and subclasses of the international classification into which the goods incorporating the designs belong.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requires Offices to record and (where published) show classification numbers on official registries and publications (Article 2(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Care in selecting terms for alphabetical list to avoid exclusive-rights terms
rubrics_metrics.description: In selecting terms for inclusion in the alphabetical list of goods, the Committee of Experts shall exercise reasonable care to avoid using terms in which exclusive rights may exist; inclusion is not an expression of opinion on whether a word is subject to exclusive rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Committee should avoid implying trademark/patent exclusivity by term selection; mere inclusion does not indicate a legal stance (Article 2(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee of Experts composition and representation
rubrics_metrics.description: A Committee of Experts shall be entrusted with tasks related to the classification; each country of the Special Union shall be represented on the Committee of Experts, organized according to rules of procedure adopted by a simple majority of countries represented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every member country has representation; the Committee adopts its own rules by simple majority (Article 3(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption of alphabetical list and notes by simple majority
rubrics_metrics.description: The Committee of Experts shall adopt the alphabetical list and explanatory notes by a simple majority of the votes of the countries of the Special Union.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most Committee decisions concerning lists/notes require only a simple majority (Article 3(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may propose amendments and timing for proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals for amendments or additions to the international classification may be made by the Office of any country of the Special Union or by the International Bureau; proposals from Offices and the International Bureau shall be transmitted to Committee members not later than two months before the session at which they will be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is a two-month transmission deadline for proposed amendments to allow review prior to Committee sessions (Article 3(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision rule for Committee amendments and unanimity for major changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions of the Committee concerning adoption of amendments and additions shall be by a simple majority; nevertheless, if such decisions entail the setting up of a new class or any transfer of goods from one class to another, unanimity shall be required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Routine changes: simple majority; structural/class transfers: require unanimity among members (Article 3(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to vote by mail in Committee
rubrics_metrics.description: Each expert shall have the right to vote by mail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remote (mail) voting is expressly permitted for Committee members (Article 3(5)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Deemed acceptance where no representation or no vote
rubrics_metrics.description: If a country does not appoint a representative for a given session, or if the appointed expert has not expressed his vote during the session or within a period to be prescribed by the rules of procedure, the country concerned shall be considered to have accepted the decision of the Committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to participate or vote within prescribed period constitutes acceptance of Committee decisions (Article 3(6)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication and entry into force of Committee decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The alphabetical list of goods and explanatory notes adopted by the Committee, as well as any amendment or addition to the international classification decided by the Committee, shall be communicated to the Offices by the International Bureau; the decisions shall enter into force as soon as the communication is received, except that decisions entailing the setting up of a new class or transfer of goods shall enter into force within six months from the date of communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The International Bureau notifies Offices; normal amendments effective on receipt, but structural class changes have a six-month delayed entry into force to allow adjustment (Article 4(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: International Bureau as depositary and publisher of amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau, as depositary of the international classification, shall incorporate amendments and additions which have entered into force and shall publish announcements of the amendments and additions in periodicals designated by the Assembly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The International Bureau maintains the official classification text and ensures dissemination of changes (Article 4(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assembly membership and delegation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Special Union shall have an Assembly consisting of the countries of the Special Union; each Government shall be represented by one delegate, who may be assisted by alternates, advisors, and experts; the expenses of each delegation are borne by the Government which appointed it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Representation at the Assembly is one delegate per country; delegations fund their own costs (Article 5(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assembly functions and powers
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to Article 3, the Assembly shall deal with matters concerning maintenance and development of the Special Union and implementation of the Agreement; give directions to the International Bureau concerning preparation for conferences of revision; review and approve Director General reports on the Special Union; determine the program and adopt the biennial budget and final accounts; adopt financial regulations; decide on establishment of official texts in other languages; establish additional committees/working groups; determine observers; adopt amendments to Articles 5 to 8; and take other appropriate actions to further objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Assembly has broad governance, budgetary, and supervisory responsibilities (Article 5(2)(a)(i)-(xi)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination with other Unions
rubrics_metrics.description: With respect to matters also of interest to other Unions administered by the Organization, the Assembly shall make decisions after hearing advice of the Coordination Committee of the Organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inter-Union coordination is required when issues overlap several Unions (Article 5(2)(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Voting and quorum in the Assembly
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Each country member has one vote. (b) One-half of the countries members shall constitute a quorum. (c) If representation is >= one-third but < one-half, the Assembly may make decisions which take effect only after absent members are invited to express their vote or abstention in writing within three months and the conditions to attain quorum and required majority are met. (d) Decisions of the Assembly shall require two-thirds of the votes cast (subject to Article 8(2)). (e) Abstentions shall not be considered votes. (f) A delegate may represent and vote in the name of one country only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed quorum and supermajority rules govern Assembly decisions; special procedure if quorum not met at session (Article 5(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assembly meeting schedule and extraordinary sessions
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) The Assembly shall meet once every second calendar year in ordinary session upon convocation by the Director General and normally during the same period and place as the General Assembly of the Organization. (b) The Assembly shall meet in extraordinary session upon convocation by the Director General at the request of one-fourth of the countries members. (c) The agenda of each session shall be prepared by the Director General.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ordinary biennial sessions are the norm; extraordinary sessions require one-fourth of members to request convocation (Article 5(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assembly's rules of procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The Assembly shall adopt its own rules of procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural autonomy for internal governance is granted to the Assembly (Article 5(5)).

rubrics_metrics.name: International Bureau administrative tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative tasks concerning the Special Union shall be performed by the International Bureau; in particular, it shall prepare meetings and provide the secretariat of the Assembly, the Committee of Experts, and other committees/working groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The International Bureau is the administrative engine for the Special Union (Article 6(1)(a)-(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Director General as chief executive and representation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director General shall be the chief executive of the Special Union and shall represent the Special Union.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director General leads and represents the Special Union in official capacities (Article 6(1)(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation of Director General and staff without vote
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director General and any staff member designated by him shall participate, without the right to vote, in all meetings of the Assembly, the Committee of Experts, and other committees or working groups; the Director General or a designated staff member shall be ex officio secretary of those bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The International Bureau's staff may attend and serve as secretariat but do not vote (Article 6(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: International Bureau's role in revision conferences
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau shall, in accordance with Assembly directions, prepare conferences of revision (other than Articles 5 to 8); it may consult intergovernmental and international non-governmental organizations concerning preparations; the Director General and designated persons shall take part without the right to vote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Bureau coordinates revision preparations and may consult external organizations (Article 6(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget composition and financing sources
rubrics_metrics.description: The Special Union shall have a budget including income and expenses proper to the Special Union, its contribution to common Union expenses, and, where applicable, the sum to the Conference of the Organization; the budget shall be financed from: (i) contributions of countries of the Special Union; (ii) fees and charges for services rendered by the International Bureau; (iii) sale of or royalties on publications; (iv) gifts, bequests, and subventions; (v) rents, interests, and other miscellaneous income.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget items and financing sources are enumerated; coordination with other Unions' budgets required (Article 7(1)-(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of national contributions tied to Paris Union class
rubrics_metrics.description: For establishing its contribution each country of the Special Union shall belong to the same class as it belongs to in the Paris Union for the Protection of Industrial Property, and shall pay its annual contributions on the basis of the same number of units as is fixed for that class in that Union.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contribution classes mirror Paris Union classifications and unit counts (Article 7(4)(a)-(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Due date for contributions and voting consequences of arrears
rubrics_metrics.description: Contributions become due on the first of January of each year; a country in arrears in payment may not exercise its right to vote in any organ of the Special Union if arrears equal or exceed contributions due for the preceding two full years, unless an organ allows continued voting when delay is due to exceptional circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely payment is linked to voting rights; exceptions possible at the organ's discretion (Article 7(4)(c)-(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget default rule if not adopted
rubrics_metrics.description: If the budget is not adopted before the beginning of a new financial period, it shall be at the same level as the budget of the previous year, as provided in the financial regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuity provision prevents funding gaps if a new budget isn't adopted (Article 7(4)(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment and reporting of fees and charges
rubrics_metrics.description: The amount of the fees and charges due for services rendered by the International Bureau in relation to the Special Union shall be established, and reported to the Assembly, by the Director General.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director General sets service fees subject to Assembly reporting (Article 7(5)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Working capital fund provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Special Union shall have a working capital fund constituted by a single payment made by each country; if insufficient the Assembly shall decide to increase it. The initial payment or participation in increases shall be a proportion of the contribution of that country for the year in which the fund is established or increase is decided; proportion and terms fixed by the Assembly on the Director General's proposal after advice of the Coordination Committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Working capital funding is proportional to country contributions and subject to Assembly decisions (Article 7(6)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Headquarters advance provision
rubrics_metrics.description: In the headquarters agreement, it shall be provided that whenever the working capital fund is insufficient, the host country shall grant advances; amounts and conditions are subject to separate agreements; either the host country or the Organization may denounce the obligation to grant advances with three years' effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host-state advance mechanisms are contractual and denounceable (Article 7(7)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit of accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Auditing of the accounts shall be effected by one or more countries of the Special Union or by external auditors, as provided in the financial regulations; they shall be designated, with their agreement, by the Assembly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assembly designates auditors per financial regulations (Article 7(8)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment procedure for Articles 5 to 8
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals to amend Articles 5, 6, 7, and the present Article may be initiated by any country or by the Director General and shall be communicated at least six months in advance to the countries; amendments shall be adopted by the Assembly requiring three-fourths of votes cast, provided that amendments to Article 5 and that paragraph shall require four-fifths; entry into force occurs one month after written notifications of acceptance by three-fourths of member countries are received, with binding and financial-obligation rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Higher majorities and acceptance procedures apply to Articles 5-8; amendments increasing financial obligations bind only accepting countries (Article 8(1)-(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ratification, accession and deposit of instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: Any country party to the Paris Convention which has signed this Agreement may ratify it, and if it has not signed may accede to it; instruments of ratification and accession shall be deposited with the Director General.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paris Convention membership is a prerequisite; deposit with Director General formalizes ratification/accession (Article 9(1)-(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry into force timing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) With respect to the first five countries which deposit instruments, the Agreement enters into force three months after deposit of the fifth instrument. (b) For any other country, the Agreement enters into force three months after the Director General notifies its ratification or accession, unless a later date is indicated in the instrument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial entry requires five ratifications/accessions; subsequent entrants follow the three-month rule (Article 9(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of ratification or accession
rubrics_metrics.description: Ratification or accession shall automatically entail acceptance of all clauses and admission to all the advantages of this Agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No partial acceptance: accession implies full acceptance of the Agreement's provisions (Article 9(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Force and duration linked to Paris Convention
rubrics_metrics.description: This Agreement shall have the same force and duration as the Paris Convention for the Protection of Industrial Property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Temporal legal effect matches that of the Paris Convention (Article 10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision of certain Articles by conference
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles 1 to 4 and 9 to 15 may be submitted to revision with a view to desired improvements; every revision shall be considered at a conference held among delegates of the countries of the Special Union.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Major content Articles may be revised via conference of delegates (Article 11(1)-(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Denunciation procedure and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Any country may denounce the Agreement by notification to the Director General; denunciation affects only the denouncing country, takes effect one year after receipt, and may not be exercised before five years of membership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawal is possible but delayed and subject to minimum membership period (Article 12(1)-(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application to territories
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of Article 24 of the Paris Convention shall apply to this Agreement (territories).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Territorial application follows Paris Convention rules (Article 13).

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature, language authenticity, deposit and transmission of copies
rubrics_metrics.description: The Agreement shall be signed in a single copy in English and French, both texts equally authentic, and deposited with Government of Switzerland; official texts in other languages established by Director General after consultation; Director General shall transmit two certified copies to Governments and register the Agreement with the UN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signature and archival formalities: bilingual equally authentic originals, deposit in Switzerland, certified copies to signatories, UN registration (Article 14(1)-(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Director General notifications role
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director General shall notify Governments of all countries members of the Special Union of the date of entry into force of the Agreement, signatures, deposits of instruments of ratification or accession, acceptances of amendments and dates of entry into force, and notifications of denunciation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director General is the official notifier of status changes and procedural milestones (Article 14(5)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional provision prior to first Director General
rubrics_metrics.description: Until the first Director General assumes office, references to the International Bureau or the Director General shall be deemed references to the United International Bureaux for the Protection of Intellectual Property (BIRPI) or its Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Temporary administrative substitution applies in the Agreement's initial period (Article 15).
